checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is Bloom filter deserialization enforcing exactly 256 bytes length validation at P2P boundary?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify all P2P message handlers that deserialize Bloom filter data (commonly in block headers, receipts, or log-related messages). 2. Trace the deserialization path for the Bloom (Bytes256) type alias. 3. Attempt to send P2P messages containing Bloom values with incorrect lengths: (a) 0 bytes (empty), (b) 255 bytes (one less than required), (c) 257 bytes (one more than required), (d) 512 bytes (double the required length), (e) 1 byte (minimal). 4. Verify that ALL malformed Bloom values are rejected BEFORE being processed by consensus logic. 5. Confirm rejection happens at the deserialization boundary, not in downstream components. 6. Verify error handling does not leak information, cause panics, or enable resource exhaustion. 7. Confirm no partial state changes occur when invalid Bloom data is received.
checklist.property_statement: The Bloom type alias MUST enforce exactly 256 bytes (Bytes256). Any deserialized Bloom value with length != 256 bytes MUST be rejected.
checklist.falsification_strategy: Craft P2P network messages with Bloom fields containing byte arrays of incorrect lengths (0, 1, 255, 257, 512 bytes) and verify they are rejected at the deserialization boundary without causing crashes, memory corruption, or state inconsistencies.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0030. Bloom filters in Ethereum are 2048 bits (256 bytes) and are used in block headers and receipts for efficient log filtering. A malformed Bloom from P2P could cause buffer overflows, incorrect log filtering, or consensus issues if length is not strictly validated at the trust boundary.

checklist.title: Falsification Test: Can the 256-byte length invariant for Bloom be violated through any code path?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate the Bloom type alias definition (should be Bytes256 or equivalent fixed-size array type). 2. Verify the type enforces exactly 256 bytes via either: (a) fixed-size array type [u8; 256], (b) newtype wrapper with validation in constructor, (c) deserialization bounds checking in serde/RLP/SSZ implementations. 3. Trace all constructors and factory functions for Bloom type. 4. Verify no unsafe conversions allow arbitrary-length byte slices to become Bloom values. 5. Check all deserialization implementations (RLP, SSZ, JSON) for length validation. 6. Verify the invariant holds across all Bloom instances: len(bloom) == 256 at all times. 7. Test encoding/decoding roundtrips preserve the 256-byte length constraint.
checklist.property_statement: The Bloom type alias MUST enforce exactly 256 bytes (Bytes256). Any deserialized Bloom value with length != 256 bytes MUST be rejected.
checklist.falsification_strategy: Attempt to construct a Bloom value with != 256 bytes through all available code paths (constructors, deserialization, type coercion, unsafe casts) and verify the type system prevents or rejects all such attempts.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0030. Supporting check for internal type safety. If the type alias does not strictly enforce length, boundary validation alone may be insufficient - internal code could inadvertently create invalid Bloom values.
